full_judgment: 3. Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing to support the rule has taken two contentions. One is that the Election Tribunal fell into an error by simply recounting the ballot papers without referring to the corresponding Ballot Paper Accounts in Form N prepared on the spot and in presence of the parties by the Presiding Officers. According to the Ballot Paper-Accounts the total number of valid ballot papers was 6605 but according to the Tribunal It was 6608 I.e. 3 ballot papers having been found in excess. Mr. Ahmed has contended that since these three ballot papers were not accounted for the natural presumption would be that these ballot papers were inserted in to the sealed packets after they were dispatched by the Presiding Officer. The details of the recounting show that in Rampur (Primary School) polling station the respondent's total of votes increased by 2 votes ehaeutia 'primary School) polling station. It Increased by 1 vote awl in Bagmara (Primary School) polling station it increased by 1 vote, whereas in one of these polling stations namely, Ghagusla, the petitioner's number of votes decreased by 1 vote. In other words if there had been any insertion of ballot papers as alleged, it was made In the sealed packets of ballot papers of all the three polling stations.
